gap: No result ChatGPT got states that every 16-inch MacBook Pro can run two or more external screens without a driver: Apple lists two for the M1 Pro (2021) and three for the M5 Pro. The one-screen limit ChatGPT warned about applies to base M1 and M2 Macs, and none of those is a 16-inch laptop. Mobile Pixels' Trio 3 Pro manual (quoted in Macworld's review) says no driver is needed when the laptop has two DP-enabled USB-C ports.
standout_why: I read four pages. The Office Journal 16-inch guide and the WorkCocoon 16-inch guide say only that a USB-C port must support DisplayPort Alt Mode. Neither mentions MacBook display limits, DisplayLink, MST, or how many ports a two-screen extender needs. iTechGuides' 2026 15-best list (cited) says MacBook support 'cannot be reduced to yes or no' and depends on chip generation, but gives no count for any Mac. Its only M1/M2/M3 mention is the ZUMWALT P7 listing's cable note. iTechGuides' 2025 guide (cited) says Trio 3 Pro uses 'two USB-C ports' but not when a driver is needed. ChatGPT's answer warned that 'some MacBooks' can't drive two screens but did not say which. No rival page connects the screen count to a 16-inch laptop.
decides: On a 16-inch MacBook Pro, a two-screen extender runs driver-free over two cables, so a driver-only triple loses its usual advantage there. Our records list the FOPO S788 as needing FOPO's UsbDisplay driver. The base-M1/M2 one-screen warning applies to 13-inch Airs, not to this question. On a 16-inch Windows laptop the deciding check is still whether it has two USB-C ports with DisplayPort Alt Mode. I could not open the FOPO pages to say which FOPO dual model needs what, so the S11 and S9G video-path cells should come from our existing records.

findings.product: general (Apple MacBook Pro 16-inch, 2021, M1 Pro / M1 Max)
findings.label: External displays supported
findings.value: M1 Pro: up to 2 external displays (6K 60 Hz). M1 Max: up to 3 at 6K plus 1 at 4K
findings.source_title: MacBook Pro (16-inch, 2021) - Technical Specifications - Apple Support
findings.note: This is the oldest Apple-silicon 16-inch MacBook Pro, and even its lowest chip drives two screens natively.

findings.product: general (Apple MacBook Pro 16-inch, current, M5 Pro / M5 Max)
findings.label: External displays supported
findings.value: M5 Pro: up to 3. M5 Max: up to 4, over any mix of Thunderbolt 5 and HDMI, or all from one Thunderbolt port
findings.note: Apple's spec page lists only M5 Pro and M5 Max for the 16-inch. The 14-inch base M6 is listed with up to 2.

findings.label: External displays supported
findings.value: Up to 2 external displays, with the built-in display also on
findings.note: Context only: the current base-chip Air drives two. There is no 16-inch Air (the largest is 15-inch).

findings.label: How Apple frames the display count
findings.value: The number of displays 'depends on your Mac model and the resolution and refresh rate of each display'
findings.source_title: How many displays can be connected to MacBook Pro - Apple Support
findings.note: This index page links to per-chip pages and gives no counts itself.

findings.label: When no driver is needed
findings.value: No driver install if the laptop has 'two DP enabled USB-C ports'. Macworld's reviewer reads this as at least one USB-C/Thunderbolt port on each side, and says the screens connect with the two included USB-C cables
findings.source_title: Mobile Pixels Trio 3 Pro review - Macworld (Simon Jary, 2026-04-02)
findings.note: Simon Jary quotes the Mobile Pixels manual. I did not open the manual itself.

findings.label: Macs that need the driver
findings.value: Base M1 and M2 Macs and the MacBook Neo can connect only one monitor, so they need Mobile Pixels' free display software. M1/M2/M3 Pro and Max, and M4/M5 Macs, run both screens without it
findings.source_title: Mobile Pixels Trio 3 Pro review - Macworld (Simon Jary, 2026-04-02)
findings.note: Named reviewer's statement. Tested on a 14-inch MacBook Pro.

findings.label: MacBook fit range
findings.source_title: Mobile Pixels Trio 3 Pro review - Macworld (Simon Jary, 2026-04-02)
findings.note: Macworld's statement of the fit range. Our record has Mobile Pixels' own range as 15–16-inch laptops.
